long_biography.plain_text:
After graduating from Rutgers, Runsdorf worked in sales and operations at generic-drug manufacturers. He established Woodfield Distribution in 2010 as a third-party logistics provider for pharmaceutical and healthcare companies. Four years later, he expanded into contract manufacturing by acquiring Pernix Manufacturing and creating Woodfield Pharmaceutical. The businesses handled warehousing, fulfillment, packaging, regulatory support and liquid-drug production.

For seven years, Runsdorf used Woodfield Pharmaceutical's Houston facility in a counterfeit cough-syrup scheme. He pleaded guilty in 2022 to conspiracy, trafficking in counterfeit drugs and money-laundering conspiracy. A federal judge subsequently sentenced him to 72 months' imprisonment and ordered $5 million forfeited. The FDA then permanently debarred him from serving companies with approved or pending drug applications. Woodfield Distribution later dissolved, closing the founder-led pharmaceutical platform.
